extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers looking up Stephen E. Ambrose or his work
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic (Wikipedia) biography summarizing Stephen E. Ambrose's life, career, writings, honors, controversies (plagiarism/fabrication), and reception. The page aggregates biographical facts, review judgments, and criticisms about his scholarship and public activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism / proper attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2002, several instances of plagiarism were discovered in his books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes multiple books contained plagiarized passages and that a Forbes investigation traced the pattern back to his doctoral dissertation. This functions as an anti-pattern: published historical work must properly attribute sources and avoid text appropriation; failure to do so undermines credibility and can be exposed by investigative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fabrication of interviews and events
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2010, after his death, Ambrose was found to have fabricated interviews and events in his biographies of Eisenhower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambrose claimed “hundreds and hundreds of hours” of interviews with Eisenhower, but presidential library records showed the pair met only three times for fewer than five hours total. The page treats fabrication or exaggeration of source access as a severe breach of historical ethics and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of oral histories and collection practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eisenhower Center collected more than 1,200 oral histories from World War II veterans; Ambrose used extensive oral histories for works such as Band of Brothers and Citizen Soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral histories can be a rich primary-source base for popular military history. The page implies good practice includes systematic collection and preservation (the Center's efforts) but also suggests the need for careful corroboration and documentation when relying on veterans' recollections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and avoidance of significant errors or fabricated quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing Like It in the World was criticized by railroad historians and journal reviewers for containing more than sixty significant errors, misstatements, and fabricated quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article treats factual accuracy and avoidance of invented quotations as core standards; failures lead to scholarly criticism and damage to reputation. Reviewers and specialists are cited as detecting and cataloguing such errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness in coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer for the Journal of Military History commended D-Day as the 'most comprehensive discussion' of the sea, air, and land operations that coalesced on that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensiveness — covering all relevant dimensions of an event (sea, air, land) — is presented as a positive evaluative quality for military-history works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability, balance, and insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Gordon Harrison (New York Times) praised Ambrose's Eisenhower work as able to 'fight through the memoranda... to uncover the idiosyncratic people at its center' and characterized his writing as penetrating, readable, lively, balanced and insightful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary qualities — readability, narrative vividness, balance, and insight — are treated as desirable features in biographical and popular-history writing, enhancing accessibility and critical reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in biographical treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Ambrose was a strong critic of Nixon, the biography was 'considered fair and just regarding Nixon's presidency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when authors hold critical views, biographies are expected to be fair and just in treatment of subjects; perceived fairness contributes to the scholarly and public credibility of a biographical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous verification of historical claims (avoid disputed/uncorroborated primacy claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Band of Brothers received criticism for its disputed claim that Easy Company was the first Allied unit to reach Berchtesgaden and Kehlsteinhaus — a distinction also claimed by elements of the 3rd Infantry Division and the French 2nd Armored Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of 'firsts' or primacy require careful corroboration and acknowledgment of competing claims; making definitive assertions without strong evidence invites dispute from other historians and primary-source records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for academic honors and appointments (national/international distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Boyd Professor of History honor is given only to faculty who attain 'national or international distinction for outstanding teaching, research, or other creative achievement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic distinctions are evaluated against standards of national/international impact across teaching, research, or creative work; the Wikipedia entry cites this as the basis for Ambrose's Boyd Professorship and thus as an explicit evaluative standard for such honors.
